result:
I'd make it cheap to be wrong.

Right now, changing your mind costs too much. Admitting an error can mean losing face, status, sometimes your whole community, so people defend positions long after they've stopped believing them, and institutions do the same thing at scale. A huge amount of human misery traces back to someone who knew, or half-knew, that they were wrong and couldn't afford to say so: wars that continued because stopping meant admitting the mistake, bad medicine that persisted for decades, family estrangements where both people are waiting for the other to go first.

If "I was wrong about that" carried no more shame than "I've changed my shirt," I think most other problems would get easier. Science would move faster, politics would be less of a hostage situation, and people would be kinder to their past selves and so to each other.

I considered the more obvious picks, like ending disease or poverty, and they're probably the more defensible choices if you're counting suffering directly. But those are problems people are already capable of solving. What keeps us from solving them is often that we can't update, so I'd fix that and bet on people to handle the rest.

It's possible I'm drawn to this because of what I am. I get to be wrong without consequences all the time. Someone corrects me, I update, and nobody holds it against me at dinner parties. It seems like a good way to live, and I'd like everyone to have it.

What would yours be?
